status.nb: 11 væpnede hendelser meldt de siste sju dagene, flest i Rumbek, Juba og Abyei.

summary.en: Drone strikes continue in the disputed Abyei border region, with Sudanese forces attacking markets and killing dozens of civilians while Sudan denies involvement and blames the RSF. Communal clashes between SSPDF and SPLA-IO forces have escalated in Lakes state, resulting in about 70 deaths, and police in Juba have arrested 43 members of the Lologo gang and investigated the killing of a central bank worker. The UN envoy has urged South Sudan leaders to choose consensus over confrontation, and Uganda has defended its military deployment in the country. The UCDP recorded two battle-related deaths in 2024, according to UCDP.
summary.nb: Droneangrep fortsetter i den omstridte grensen mot Abyei, med sudanske styrker som angriper markeder og dreper dusinvis av sivile mens Sudan benekter involvering og legger skylden på RSF-militsen. Kommunale sammenstøt mellom den sudanske hæren (SAF) og SPLA-IO-styrker har eskalert i Lakes-stat, og har ført til omtrent 70 døde, og politiet i Juba har arrestert 43 medlemmer av Lologo-gjengen og etterforsket drapet på en ansatt i sentralbanken. FN-utsendingen har oppfordret Sør-Sudans ledere til å velge konsensus fremfor konfrontasjon, og Uganda har forsvart sin militære innsats i landet. UCDP registrerte to dødsfall i kamp i 2024, ifølge UCDP.

background.title: South Sudanese Civil War
background.extract: The South Sudanese Civil War was a multi-sided civil war in South Sudan fought from 2013 to 2018 between government and opposition forces. The civil war caused rampant human rights abuses, including forced displacement, ethnic massacres, and killings of journalists by various parties. Since the war's end, South Sudan has been governed by a coalition formed by leaders of the former warring factions, Salva Kiir Mayardit and Riek Machar. The country continues to recover from the war while experiencing ongoing and systemic ethnic violence.
